comparison: Perfect agreement on study design and methodology (C32-C38). Both evaluations find the cohort characterization, technical approach, and validation methods well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly noted the methodological rigor as a strength.

Complete agreement on variant detection and validation (C39-C46). Both evaluations accept the high ddPCR confirmation rates and cell-type specificity. Peer reviewers highlighted the extensive molecular validation as a strength.

Strong agreement on overall mutational burden patterns (C47-C51, with peer also including C52). Both evaluations support the age correlation and blood SNV findings. Peer reviewers noted the careful separation of microglia SNVs from clonal hematopoiesis.

Agreement on pathogenic variant enrichment in AD microglia (C53-C59), though peer review also includes C3, C60-C61. Both acknowledge statistical significance while noting modest cohort size. Peer reviewers stated evidence is 'compelling' but acknowledged small sample size limitations.

OpenEval addresses negative control evidence (C60-C61) separately, while peer review groups this with the main enrichment findings (C3, C53-C61). Both evaluations support the specificity demonstrated by these controls.

Strong agreement on MAPK pathway enrichment and CBL recurrence (C62-C67, C70). Both evaluations find the pathway analysis and recurrent mutations compelling. Peer reviewers emphasized the 'striking enrichment' and agreement between methods.

Agreement on functional validation of variant pathogenicity (C68-C69). Both evaluations support the ERK phosphorylation data. OpenEval notes HEK293T cell limitation, while peer reviewers accept the validation across multiple systems as convincing.

OpenEval addresses allelic frequency context (C71-C72) while peer review groups these with broader conclusions (C70-C93). Both evaluations support the histiocytosis comparison and allelic frequency interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates mouse cell line data (C73-C75) separately, while peer review groups functional validation across systems (C68-C69, C73-C74). Both support the findings but OpenEval explicitly notes BV2 cell line limitations.

Agreement on iPSC-derived human cell validation (C76-C79). OpenEval notes 'slightly increased' proliferation suggests modest effects, while peer reviewers emphasize the convincing nature of over-activation across multiple systems including human microglia-like cells.

Strong agreement on inflammatory responses (C80-C85). Both evaluations support the transcriptional and protein-level findings. Peer reviewers highlighted the pro-inflammatory phenotype as convincingly demonstrated across systems.

Perfect claim overlap (C86-C89) but different evaluation outcomes. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to small sample size (n=2 variant carriers) and difficulty distinguishing cause vs. effect. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, emphasizing concordance between in vitro and patient data as a strength.

Agreement on main findings (C3-C5, C90-C92) with appropriate caution. OpenEval notes 'promote' language implies causation requiring longitudinal data. Peer reviewers emphasized careful conclusions and acknowledgment that findings may explain a subset of AD patients.

OpenEval addresses sufficiency claim (C93) separately, noting 'sufficient' is strong language given in vitro limitations. Peer review groups this with broader conclusions, accepting the multi-faceted approach as compelling.
Agreement on literature contextualization (C94-C96). Both evaluations accept these citations to prior work. Peer reviewers noted the MAPK-AD connection and BRAF mouse model provide important context.
Agreement on biological context through literature (C97-C101). Both evaluations support these contextual claims. OpenEval notes these are primarily literature-based rather than new findings.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding MAPK-APOE4 relationship (C102-C103). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting non-significant findings and insufficient sample size. Peer review groups with other observations but accepts the careful analysis.

Agreement on local origin of microglial variants (C104-C106). Both evaluations support the interpretation that variants arise locally rather than from peripheral infiltration. Peer reviewers noted the careful separation from clonal hematopoiesis.

Agreement on distinction between pathogenic variants and general burden (C107-C108). Both evaluations support the specificity of P-SNV enrichment. OpenEval notes appropriate caution about causality given cross-sectional design.
Agreement on negative finding regarding AD pathological features (C109). Both evaluations accept this result while noting limited statistical power for subgroup analysis.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty regarding temporal dynamics and causality (C8-C9, C28, C110-C113). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN, noting cross-sectional design cannot distinguish cause from consequence. Peer reviewers explicitly stated 'this study cannot conclude whether microglial mosaic mutations cause AD or are an effect of AD.'

Strong agreement on background and contextual claims (C1-C2, C10-C31, C33, C52 in OpenEval; similar set in peer review). Both evaluations support these literature-based claims. Peer reviewers validated the framing and rationale as sound.
